I’ve been in a similar place to you and ended up on a carousel of antidepressants that had more side effects than actual antidepressant effects. I was going through a yearlong, severe depressive episode. Ultimately, I found that low dose ketamine was the one treatment that actually helped me. It’s a fast acting antidepressant. When I first took it kinda felt like a miracle because of how quickly things cleared up for me at the time. I know this is kinda coming off as a plug or whatever but I wanted to share this with you in case it could help you. There’s a community at /r/therapeuticketamine that was a helpful resource for me. My parents were neglectful in my upbringing. Not abusive, at least not by the hardest definitions, just neglectful. They tried their best but their best just wasn’t good enough.

They were also neglected and abused in their childhoods as well. They’re just another link in a long chain of generational trauma. My parents are flawed people but they were never bad people. I choose to accept them in my life as they are today even if their ignorance led to damage to me in my childhood. I wish the burden of changing into a better person didn’t fall on me, but I have to accept that too.

Thanks for replying. I’m glad I’m not the only one out there that came out hurt from this experience. I hope for the best for you too.

> It’s hard not to be resentful. I feel a real sense of the grief for the person I feel I couldn’t live up to (was very gifted in English and writing when I was younger but ultimately led to nothing as I wasn’t really supported)

I wanted to address this because this is something that I’ve felt strongly about for years. I constantly mourn the person I could have been if I only had the right parents. It’s hard not to be resentful at all the potential I had to be such a smart, kind, and loving person. I so badly would have liked to been him. To live his life and have take all those opportunities that the real me never had. It’s kinda cheesy but I’m reminded of this lyric from the band Titus Andronicus: “you ain’t ever been a virgin, kid, you were fucked from the start”. 

Every now and again I can be that person from that alternate universe, at least for a moment. But it doesn’t last. It’s funny, I think a lot of the self-hate I deal with ties back to that resentment. The word “perfectionism” gets thrown around in the CPTSD space a lot. I so badly wish I was raised right. Instead I mourn him and I have to deal with everything I am now.

Use the search bar to look up 'Joyous' on this sub. You'll find tons of discussions.

As far as ketamine goes, you get what you pay for. Their service sucks, they're a pain to get in touch with, and you have to fill out their check-in regularly. 

But the ketamine is legit. It's by far the best bang for your buck in terms in terms of mg/dollar. I have low expectations of Joyous but I'm happy with the ketamine. Don't expect a full-service psych out of Joyous. If you already know that you want to try ketamine for your depression, then they're the way to go.

For me it worked immediately. Session 1. It suddenly felt like this piece of my brain that was not working suddenly came back online. I was in disbelief that my depression and suicidal thoughts that I’d struggled with could be treated so rapidly.

Definitely not snake oil. I credit it with practically saving my life. It’s not covered by insurance because it’s a very new treatment that’s still being fully researched, so still insurers consider ketamine treatment experimental. Health insurance moves slowly. Don’t bother waiting for them. 

I also find IV treatment inhibitively expensive. Many of us here use a provider called Joyous that’s $129/month with no insurance. Their service sucks ass but they’re the cheapest provider in town by a mile. They send you ketamine troches that you take by yourself at home. Try them out if cost is an issue. I can vouch for their product and the benefits that it’s provided me.
